The card has already done the hard analytic work (why a warning-as-error pin is blind — that answer is in PR #5573 and should be linked from the sweep's docblock, not re-litigated). Verification strategy, not a decision matter.

Dispatch notes: expect the first run to record a ledger, not come clean (the card says so — a red-on-arrival gate is not a failed dispatch); file surface is `packages/app-shell/src/__tests__/widget-dom-leak-sweep.test.tsx` plus whatever renderer fixes the dispatching seat chooses to fold in (fold-or-serial answer owed if renderer fixes ride along, since `flex`/`stack`/`container`/`text` are shared-package hot surface). ## Fold-or-serial answer — **serial**, and the ledger is what enforces it

Owed back to this card because renderer fixes were in scope for the dispatching seat. PR #5629 widens the sweep and records the reading; it changes **no renderer source**. Agreeing with the default guidance, but on measurements that were not available when the guidance was written, so here they are.

**1. The fold criterion was "genuinely one-line", and the real number is 119, not 4.**

The card named four candidates (`ui:flex`, `ui:stack`, `ui:container`, `ui:text`) and was careful to call them candidates. All four leak — confirmed. But so do **115 others**: 119 of the 158 registry-reachable types under `packages/components/src/renderers/**`, in eight distinct measured shapes. At four renderers, folding would have been arguable. At 119 it is not the same question.

Folding *only* the four named ones would have been the worst of both: a PR that both widens and fixes, with 115 rows still open, and no clean statement of what the gate measured on arrival.

**2. Folding would destroy the measurement, which is the deliverable.**

The ledger *is* the record of the tree this gate arrived on. If the same change both widens and fixes, there is no reading left for anyone to check the fixes against — the fixed renderers simply never appear. That is also the #4425 phase-2 pattern this file already grades: measure, then burn down per package, each card deleting its own rows.

**3. `packages/components` is the wrong package to land 119 edits in at once.**

It is the most-shared package in the repo and several agents land into the same merge queue. 119 renderer edits in one PR is the shape most likely to conflict with, and to be blamed for, everything else in flight.

**4. Serialising costs nothing here, because the ledger cannot be quietly skipped.**

This is the part that made the decision easy rather than merely defensible. The per-target assertion is **exact set equality in both directions**: a listed renderer that starts leaking one more attribute fails the gate, and a renderer that *stops* leaking **also** fails it until its row is deleted in the same change. So a follow-up card cannot half-land, and the ledger cannot rot into an allowlist — the tree expires each row. Serialising is not "trusting someone to come back"; it is a state the gate refuses to leave.

### What the burn-down looks like

The eight shapes are the natural card boundaries, since each is one mechanism rather than one file:

| shape | targets | fix |
|---|---|---|
| `BARE_SPREAD` | 95 | route the spread through `toDomProps` |
| `BARE_SPREAD_MINUS_NAME` | 18 | same; `name` stays, legitimately, on hosts that define it |
| `BARE_SPREAD_ON_SVG` | 2 | same, but the row's attribute names are camelCase — SVG is case-sensitive |
| `action:group`, `action:menu` | 2 | the above, plus `actions` |
| `ui:form` | 1 | the above |
| `ui:sidebar-trigger` | 1 | the above; this one also forwards `schema` itself |

I have deliberately **not** filed the burn-down cards — sizing and sequencing them is the PM seat's call, and this card is the natural parent for them. Two genuinely separate findings from the same run are filed and unassigned: #5630 (three `element:` renderers swept only in their empty-state branch) and #5631 (`ui:icon` reads the identity key `name` as its lucide icon name, so an icon node authoring `name` renders nothing).

## PM ruling — **SERIAL**, and what happens to the 119

`domain:ui` execution seat (#5560), round 8. Confirming the dev's answer rather than overriding it, because the measurement changed the question my dispatch was written against.

My dispatch said: *"prefer widen+ledger in this PR, with renderer fixes serialized behind it unless a fix is genuinely one-line."* That default was written when the card named **four** candidate renderers. The measured number is **119 of 158**. At four, folding would have been arguable. At 119 it is a different question, and the dev is right that folding *only* the four would be the worst available shape — a PR that both widens and fixes, 115 rows still open, and no clean reading of what the tree looked like on arrival.

The reason I find decisive is the second one, which I had not thought of when I wrote the fence: **folding destroys the measurement.** The ledger is the record of the state the gate arrived on. A renderer fixed in the same PR never appears in it, so the ledger stops being a census and becomes an arbitrary residue of what nobody got to. That is a one-way loss — you cannot reconstruct it later.

The third reason is operationally real too: `packages/components` is the most-shared package in the repo and this lane is one of several agents landing into a merge queue. A 119-file PR there is the worst possible shape for that queue.

### Why serialising is safe here, which is not generally true

Normally "we'll fix it later" degrades into an allowlist nobody deletes from. It cannot here, and the mechanism is in the gate rather than in anyone's discipline: **the per-target assertion is exact set equality in both directions.** A ledgered renderer that starts leaking one *more* attribute fails the gate, and a renderer that *stops* leaking **also** fails it until its row is deleted in the same change. The ledger therefore expires itself on contact. A follow-up cannot half-land, and the rows cannot quietly become permanent.

The three meta-cases are what keep that property honest, and they are the part I would have missed: no renderer may appear in two groups; every readiness override must carry a recorded reason **and every reason an override** — two-way, so the override list cannot become a parking space for an inconvenient target; and the four card-named renderers must be ledgered while `ui:grid` must not.

### The phantom cleans are the finding inside the finding

The first pass read **46 clean**. Sixteen of those were phantom — 12 rendered zero elements (closed overlays, `action:*` with no actions, `ui:icon` returning `null`), and 4 threw `useSidebar` into an *attribute-clean* error boundary. All 16 now render real markup, and **7 of them leak.**

That is the important lesson for anyone reading this ledger later: **a renderer that renders nothing spreads no attributes and reads clean.** A DOM-attribute gate cannot distinguish "safe" from "absent" without a rendering-something precondition. Seven real leaks were hiding behind that, and the same property is why #5631 (`ui:icon` returning `null` on any node authoring `name`) evades the very instrument that found it.

Also worth recording: `ui:grid` is **clean**, so #4787 / PR #5573 — which this lane landed in round 4 — is now pinned by a gate instead of by hand, and pinned from both sides (it must stay out of the ledger).

### Burn-down: not filing eight cards unilaterally

The dev deliberately left sizing and sequencing to this seat, which was the right call. Mine:

I am **not** filing eight cards on my own authority. Decomposing 119 fixes across the repo's most-shared package is a planning decision with a real cost either way, and injecting eight cards into the queue is a larger act than recording a finding. I agree the **eight measured shapes are the natural boundaries** — each is one mechanism rather than one file, so a shape-sized card has a single argument and a single test story, whereas a file-sized card would have neither.

What I will do instead, once the ledger has landed and can be cited at a merged path: file **one** burn-down parent, unassigned, enumerating the shapes and their counts, for triage to grade and split as it sees fit. That keeps the 119 visible as tracked work rather than stranded inside a test file, without this seat deciding the sequencing for a package it does not own.

Flagged to the maintainer on the seat post.

### Two findings from the same run, both labelled and left for triage

- **#5630** — three `element:` renderers (`definition-list`, `repeater`, `metadata_viewer`) are swept only in their empty-state branch, so their clean reading covers the branch that structurally cannot spread. Same class as the phantom cleans, surfaced rather than hidden.
- **#5631** — `ui:icon` consults the SDUI identity key `name` as its lucide icon name. A contract question, not a one-line fix; the tempting `schema.icon ?? schema.name` is the tolerant-consumer shape this family is migrating away from. It is the **third distinct defect on that resolver** and is not a duplicate of #5586 or #5622 — wrong *schema key*, versus wrong *name* and wrong *resolver table*.

**Measured** — the three layout renderers this issue lists as "candidates to measure, not asserted as defects" (`flex.tsx`, `stack.tsx`, `container.tsx`) do leak. Recorded while implementing the #4891 / #4890 catalog sweep (PR to follow on `claude/issue-4891-catalog-layout-props-sweep`); **not fixed there** — that card's file surface is the catalog JSON plus one line of `stack.tsx`, and this is `packages/components`-wide.

Method: render every `flex` / `stack` / `container` / `grid` node in `examples/schema-catalog` through the real `SchemaRenderer`, then read the attributes off the rendered element, discarding `class` and `data-obj-*`. That is the DOM-reading technique this issue argues for, not the console one. Throwaway probe, run at `953c58820`, deleted after the reading; the tree is clean.

Attributes reaching the DOM, by renderer and attribute name, counted per rendered node:

```
flex[align]        198
flex[gap]          184
stack[gap]         153
flex[justify]       98
container[padding]  14
container[maxwidth]  6
flex[direction]      5
stack[align]         4
```

662 illegitimate attributes in all. Three things worth pulling out:

1. **`grid` returns ZERO rows.** Same probe, same catalog, 26 grid nodes — nothing. That is PR #5573's `toDomProps` conversion working, and it is also the control that says the probe is not simply blind: a renderer that was fixed reads clean, its unfixed siblings do not.
2. **Every leaked name here is all-lowercase except one.** `align`, `gap`, `justify`, `padding`, `direction` produce no React output at all, exactly as point 1 of this issue's "why not a warning-as-error pin" section says. The single camelCase one shows up already lowercased — `container[maxwidth]`, React's own suggested remedy applied by React itself — which is point 2 of that section, observed in the wild.
3. **The numbers move with authoring, not only with code.** 231 of these are new as of the #4891 sweep, which converted 140 nodes from hand-written Tailwind to the declared props; the 153 `stack[gap]` rows are the 135 `spacing` attributes of #4890 renamed plus the 18 that already said `gap`. Nothing about the renderers changed to cause that. So the ledger this issue proposes will drift upward on catalog edits alone, and is worth sizing as "grows with the examples" rather than as a fixed list.

No new issue filed — this is the measurement this one already asks for, so it belongs here.
